# Nirjar Goswami

> Generalist - Working across Cloud & DevOps, Cybersecurity, Backend Engineering, and System Design, with an emphasis on secure, resilient, and cost-aware infrastructure.
> Building systems meant to be forgotten. Everyone's specializing, but Nirjar went wide instead, learning how most of the pieces connect rather than mastering just one.
> Raw structured Markdown view available on site: https://nirjar.me/index.md

## About
Nirjar Goswami is a systems and security engineer working across Cloud Architecture, DevOps, Cybersecurity, and System Design. His operating principle is that infrastructure should be boring to operate: secure by default, cheap to run, observable before launch, and recoverable by plan instead of by improvisation. Every project he ships solves a problem he actually ran into - each feature exists for a reason.

## Services & What He Does
- Cybersecurity: Find it before they do. Finding weak points through testing and recon, then prioritizing, fixing, and verifying them.
- DevOps: Automate the boring parts. Automating how software is built, tested, deployed, and monitored, with safe releases and rollbacks.
- Cloud Architecture & Security: Cost-aware from day one. Designing AWS infrastructure with secure access, protected secrets, and costs under control.
- System Design: Draw it before you build it. Turning requirements into clear architecture, with failure points, scale, and cost considered early.
- Backend Development: Reliable behind the scenes. Building APIs and services that handle webhooks, events, and data reliably.
- Code Quality: Built to be maintained. Keeping code readable and maintainable with static analysis, automated tests, and Git workflows.

## How He Works
- Automate the Repeatable: Ship faster, break less. Anything done twice gets automated, so no step depends on someone remembering it.
- Fix, Don’t File: Fixed, not filed. Issues are ranked by real impact and closed, not left sitting in a backlog.
- Security from the Start: Nothing left open. It’s part of the first design conversation, not a review at the end.
- Signals Early: Know before it breaks. Systems report their own problems, so I hear about them from a dashboard, not a user.
- Recovery Planned: Fail loud, recover fast. Rollback steps are written while things are calm, not improvised mid-incident.

## How He Thinks (Mental Models)
- Systems Fluency: Where pieces connect. Built across the frontend, backend, infra, and pipeline layers, enough to see how a change in one breaks another.
- Trade-offs: Everything costs something. Each choice buys something and gives something up. I write down both before deciding.
- Simplicity: Fewer moving parts. Every extra component is one more thing to break and maintain. It earns its place or stays out.
- Accuracy over Polish: Tested, not assumed. Claims get checked before they’re trusted, including my own.
- Fault Isolation: Small blast radius. Components are scoped so one failure stays local and its cause is obvious.

## Operating Credo
> "Production systems should be boring to operate. The work goes into the architecture, the automation, and the failure modes - so when things break, recovery is a script, not a panic."

## Core Systems & Featured Works

### Trace
- Type: Digital Forensics & Incident Response
- Case Study: https://nirjar.me/works/trace
- Repository: https://github.com/nirjxr26/Trace
- Stack: Python, Typer, Rich, Textual, SQLAlchemy, SQLite, PostgreSQL, CycloneDX SBOM
- Architecture: A local-first CLI tool for managing forensic cases, proving nothing was tampered with, and updating itself without ever putting evidence at risk. Case management, tamper-proof records, and safe updates - all in one local-first CLI tool. Tracks cases from open to sealed, with cryptographic hash-chaining, tamper-evident audit logs, and isolated atomic updates with automatic rollback.

### Bastion
- Type: Self-Hosted IAM Platform
- Case Study: https://nirjar.me/works/bastion
- Repository: https://github.com/nirjxr26/Bastion
- Stack: AWS EC2, TypeScript, Python, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, JWT, Docker, Kubernetes, Helm, Terraform, ArgoCD, Datadog, Prometheus, Grafana, Loki
- Architecture: Enterprise-grade access control without handing user data to a third party. Auth, policy enforcement, MFA, session control, and audit logging in one self-hosted stack - zero third-party data access, step-up verification, scoped API keys, policy simulation against live scenarios, filterable and exportable audit logs.

### Kost
- Type: Kubernetes Cluster Cost Optimizer
- Case Study: https://nirjar.me/works/kost
- Repository: https://github.com/nirjxr26/Kost
- Stack: Go, client-go, Prometheus, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Slack Incoming Webhooks, Kubernetes, Docker
- Architecture: Compares requested CPU/memory against actual 95th-percentile utilization, outputs exact single-line kubectl patch commands, calculates dollar impact of wasted core-hours. Zero-CRD standalone binary with CI gate integration - no dashboard, no database, no bill.

### HookDrop
- Type: Real-Time Event & Webhook Ingestion Engine
- Case Study: https://nirjar.me/works/hookdrop
- Repository: https://github.com/nirjxr26/HookDrop
- Stack:Go, net/http, Zerolog, OpenTelemetry, OTLP gRPC, Docker, Kubernetes, Helm, ArgoCD, Kyverno, Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Tempo, OTel Collector, Trivy, Cosign, Renovate
- Architecture: Mock webhook receiver in Go - POST to a bucket URL, it catches, stores, and streams live. Production-grade pipeline around it: containerization, hardening, GitOps delivery, sub-35ms delivery under load.

### More Works
- DeployLens: Deployment Insights Timeline. Ties GitHub Actions and AWS CodeDeploy into a single timeline so a commit's full deployment story is visible on both sides instead of split across two dashboards. Repository: https://github.com/nirjxr26/DeployLens
- Canopy: Self-Hosted Identity & Authentication (Clerk Alternative). Argon2id password hashing, encrypted MFA, and session control users never have to think about, with zero per-user pricing. Repository: https://github.com/nirjxr26/canopy
- SmartFlow: Workflow Automation. A platform that unifies task workflows, approval pipelines, and system resource insights into a streamlined operations dashboard. Repository: https://github.com/nirjxr26/SmartFlow
- BlamLess: GitHub Action. Figures out whether a CI failure is due to user code or GitHub platform issues, and retries automatically if it's GitHub's fault. Repository: https://github.com/nirjxr26/Blamless
- Code Humanizer: AI Code Explainer Skill. Tells developers why code exists, what breaks it, and what the original author was thinking with different explanation modes. Repository: https://github.com/nirjxr26/code-humanizer
- VaultLock: Offline Password Manager. AES-256 encrypted local credential vault with desktop UI that requires zero network access. Repository: https://github.com/nirjxr26/VaultLock-Password-Manager
